title: [Bugs] UPF crashes with nil pointer dereference when processing Session Report Response for a deleted PFCP session
body: ## Bug Decription free5GC UPF may crash with a fatal nil pointer dereference when it receives a PFCP Session Report Response for a session that has already been deleted locally. In the observed case, the UPF first creates PFCP sessions normally. Then, the corresponding local session is deleted through a PFCP Session Deletion procedure. After the local session has been removed, a PFCP Session Report Response related to that deleted session arrives at the UPF. When handling this delayed or stale PFCP Session Report Response, the UPF attempts to look up the session state through the local/remote session mapping. However, because the corresponding session has already been deleted, the lookup result may be nil. The code does not properly check whether the returned session pointer is nil before dereferencing it, which causes the UPF process to panic. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Extract the attached archive. 2. Deploy the test environment using the provided docker-compose.yaml: `docker compose up -d` 3. Wait until all free5GC components are fully started. Run the provided PoC script: `python3 poc.py` 4. Observe the UPF container logs: `docker logs -f upf` ## Expected Behavior UPF should safely reject malformed or inconsistent PFCP Session Report Responses. ## Screenshots ## Environment **Please, complete the following information:** - free5GC Version: [e.g. v4.2.2] - OS: [e.g. Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS] - Kernel version: [e.g. 5.15.0-139-generic] - go version: [e.g. 1.21.8 linux/amd64] - C compiler version 9.4.0 (Ubuntu 9.4.0-1ubuntu1~20.04.2) ## Trace Files - Configuration Files - PCAP File - Log File - PoC File [VUL-20260602.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28589197/VUL-20260602.zip)
